newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee seen at 36.19 vs dlr in 6 months-poll.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee seen at 36.19 vs dlr in 6 months-poll.

text.p: The Indian rupee is seen easing to 36.19 against the dollar in six months, Standard Chartered Bank said quoting from its poll of 100 corporate treasurers,
The poll found the rupee at a mean of 35.82 against the dollar in one month, 35.90 in three months and 36.19 in six months, the bank said.
The poll was conducted in the first week of June, a bank official said.
"The poll shows that treasurers expect the rupee to be relatively stable," it said in a commentary.
"The expected rate of depreciation is significantly lower than the forecast forward premiums implying that export covers would still be a good decision," Standard Charterd said.
The rupee was quoted steady at 35.81/82 against the dollar on Friday.
The poll found the annualised dollar-rupee forward premium at a mean of 4.63 percent in one month, 5.01 percent in three months and 5.41 percent in six months.
The six month premium closed Thursday at 4.07 percent.

"The forward premiums which were expected to rise to 7.91 percent as per the pre-credit policy poll (conducted in February 1997) are expected to range between 4.63 percent and 5.41 percent over the next six months," the bank commentary said.

"This is attributed to easier liquidity conditions following the slack season credit policy," it said, referring to the Reserve Bank of India's April monetary policy which cut cash reserve requirement to boost liquidity in the banking system.
Standard Chartered Bank said the 100 treasurers were selected on the basis of their forex exposure management.
